record.one_liner: B2B customer support platform unifying Slack, Teams, email, and chat into one ticketing system with a REST API.
record.auth_notes: Main REST API uses Bearer token auth (Authorization: Bearer <token>), token created by an Admin user in the Pylon dashboard. The separate MCP server uses OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit).
record.access_notes: Docs state only Admin users can create API tokens (in-account self-serve token creation, no separate vendor application). Pylon's own pricing page has no self-serve signup/checkout, only a 'schedule a demo' funnel, and third-party sources report seat-based paid plans (Starter $59/seat/mo+) with no confirmed free tier for the core platform, so obtaining an admin account requires a paid subscription.
record.api_breadth_basis: Vendor API reference index lists 20+ resource families (Accounts & Activities, Attachments, Audit Logs, Call Recordings, Contacts, Custom Fields, Custom Objects, Feature Requests, Issues, Knowledge Base, Macros, Me, Messages, Surveys, Tags, Tasks & Projects, Teams, Ticket Forms, Training Data, User Roles, Users), each with multiple CRUD/search endpoints.
record.blocker_notes: API token creation itself is not gated by a separate approval process (any workspace Admin can self-serve create a token), but reaching Admin status requires an active paid Pylon subscription; the vendor pricing page does not expose self-serve checkout, only a demo-booking CTA.

evidence.quote: Only Admin users can create API tokens.
The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol.
